policy_title: Protect leaseholders and simplify lease extensions
stated: Reform UK will protect leaseholders by requiring all potential charges to be clearly stated and consented to, enforcing Section 106 agreements, and making it cheaper and easier to extend leases to 990 years and buy freeholds.

source.quote: Protection for Leaseholders All potential charges for leasehold or freehold residents must be clearly stated and consented to. Enforce Section 106 agreements. Ensure it is cheaper and easier to extend leases to 990 years and buy freeholds.

bearing_set.reason: The policy directly reduces the cost and friction of owning a leasehold home — cheaper lease extensions to 990 years, cheaper freehold purchase, capped/transparent service charges, and enforced Section 106 affordable-housing obligations all bear materially on housing affordability and security of tenure.

Shorter leases create depreciating, unmortgageable assets that trap leaseholder wealth and constrain economic mobility; cheaper extensions and freehold purchase restore asset value and remove a structural barrier to property-based economic opportunity — a real O13 mechanism beyond O1's housing-access frame.

membership_note: Policy is tightly focused on leasehold reform: O1 (housing affordability and security) and O13 (economic mobility and asset opportunity for leaseholders) both earn non-negligible verdicts. Service-charge transparency affects ongoing housing bills but the primary instrument is the capital transaction structure, so the housing-affordability home (O1) captures the cost dimension adequately without forcing a separate O2 bearing.
